objections.claim_attacked: hypothesis + chosen_intervention: layer adjustment 0.45→0.2 (plus 30→35 iterations) as the resolution of this failure
objections.objection: Scope mismatch between intervention and the named cause. The record's own observation localizes congestion 'around the macro' and the hypothesis separately names a GR path 'looping around the macro' many times (#5971). In the standard semantics of the parameter the record itself cites (set-global-routing-layer-adjustment), lowering 0.45 to 0.2 raises modeled track capacity globally; that plausibly lets GRT converge and 'finish', but it does not remove a path that loops a macro — it only thins per-corridor demand by giving every corridor more nominal tracks. On this record the intervention treats the completion symptom, not the loop cause, and the absent post-fix DRC count is precisely the measurement that would separate masking from repair. The draft half-acknowledges this in gaps[2] but chosen_intervention still reads as 'the fix'.

objections.claim_attacked: post_state: treating 'complete BoomTile' as a completion report
objections.objection: In the quoted sentence 'We also changed the number of congestion iterations to 35 to complete BoomTile', 'to complete BoomTile' is a purpose infinitive (in order to complete), not an attestation of a completed state; the only accomplishment claim anywhere in the record is the modal 'could finish GRT', itself ambiguous between 'we were able to' and 'it was possible to'. post_state hedges ('reported to complete') but still tallies two quoted phrases as if both witnessed completion, when one witnesses at most intent.

objections.claim_attacked: gaps[3]: 'We (eder-matheus) note the layer-adjustment is documented at set-global-routing-layer-adjustment; exact meaning of a high vs low value only explained in prose.'
objections.objection: Attribution defect inside a gaps item, not a style nit: the clause is written in the participant's voice with an extractor-style parenthetical spliced in, so it is not determinable from this record whether 'exact meaning only explained in prose' is thread content or extractor editorializing stored as record fact. This matters because the claim quietly undercuts the episode's own hypothesis — judging 0.45 'too aggressive' presumes the high/low semantics are in fact understood.

mechanism_check: Coherent where it needs to be, with one scope break. The paradox in observation — 20k congestion DRCs at 0.24 density with large open regions, especially over the die top — is internally consistent and diagnostic: at that utilization physical demand cannot plausibly oversubscribe a whole region, so the natural suspect is GRT's capacity model rather than real routing demand, and an adjustment of 0.45 (removing a large fraction of modeled tracks per layer, per the parameter's standard semantics) is exactly the kind of setting 'derived from other asap7 designs' that over-constrains a sparse design. The fix direction is right for the stated goal: lower adjustment raises modeled capacity, and a modest iteration bump (30→35) adds rip-up/reroute headroom, so intervention → 'GRT finishes' is mechanistically plausible. The chain breaks on scope: it explains completion, not elimination of the around-macro congestion if the #5971 looping behavior is real, and a lower adjustment also shrinks the safety margin the adjustment exists to provide, which can relocate rather than remove pressure at detail routing. Whether the change was merged as code, and any post-fix DRT/flow behavior: not-determinable-from-this-record.
evidence_check: post_state is asserted, not measured: two quoted phrases with, per the draft's own gaps, no post-fix DRC count, no runtime, and a not_planned/Stale automatic closure in 2026 — roughly 14 months after the 2024-11-14 comment nobody closed the issue as completed, which is itself circumstantial evidence the completion claim was never accepted or verified. A closed-out fix would have to show: post-fix GRT DRC count (ideally at or below the flow-fail threshold), GRT runtime, and a merged commit or PR setting adjustment 0.2 / iterations 35, with closure reason completed. None of that is in the record. The draft discloses the defect in gaps[0-2] rather than papering over it, so the evidence defect belongs to the thread and the episode inherits it honestly; per the rules it is scored here and not re-charged as an objection.
attribution_check: Sound on metadata: named participant (eder-matheus, role MEMBER per chosen_intervention), date 2024-11-14, locator = the issue URL; the ellipsis in chosen_intervention indicates same-comment elision, so attaching both sentences to one comment is defensible. Partial on support: the carried direct_quote text attests only the adjustment half; the iterations-35 half rests on the purpose-infinitive clause attacked in objections, and the 'could' hedge is faithfully but insufficiently carried into post_state's 'reported to complete'. The quote does support the claim chosen_intervention attaches to it in substance; it over-supports nothing beyond completion-as-claim.
missing_from_story: Whether 'finish GRT' meant zero residual congestion DRCs or merely below the flow-fail threshold — the record never says what completion implies for the 20k count, and the two readings differ in kind.

Where the 0.45 value lived (ORFS asap7 platform default vs per-design script) and whether the fix was a platform-default change or a BoomTile-local override — needed to judge the blast radius of a value 'derived from other asap7 designs'.
Design scale (instance count, macro count/dimensions, die size) so '20k' and '0.24' can be sized against the design rather than read in the abstract.
The stale-closure tension: a fix claimed working in Nov 2024 but an issue left to a not_planned/Stale close in 2026 begs why it never closed completed; a real account spends one line on this.
The downstream cost of the fix direction: lower adjustment leaves less detail-routing margin, so an account should state whether DRT or later flow stages were re-run and at what residual cost.
most_defensible_part: observation (with prior_state): the 20k-DRCs-at-0.24-density anomaly is quantitative, was reproduced through a named script (`run-me-BoomTile-asap7-base.sh gui`), is the load-bearing datum that makes both the over-aggressive-adjustment hypothesis and the fix direction coherent, and it stands independently of the unverified completion claim.
